Diallel analysis by Griffing's methods

Source: R/breeding.R
diallel.Rd

Griffing's (1956) analysis of a diallel cross by any of the four methods: 1, parents, F1 and reciprocals; 2, parents and one F1 per pair; 3, F1 and reciprocals; 4, one F1 per pair. The analysis of variance of general (GCA) and specific (SCA) combining ability, and of reciprocal effects (split into maternal and non-maternal, Cockerham 1963) in methods 1 and 3; the effects with their exact standard errors (Model I), the standard errors of differences, and the variance components of Model II with the additive and dominance variances.

Usage

diallel(
  data,
  response,
  parent1,
  parent2,
  block = NULL,
  method = 1,
  inbreeding = 1
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long format.

response

Name of the numeric response column.

parent1, parent2

Names of the female and male parent columns (equal for the parents themselves).

block

Name of the block column (randomised complete blocks); when NULL the entries are taken as completely randomised.

method

Griffing's method, 1 to 4.

inbreeding

Inbreeding coefficient of the parents, used to turn the Model II components into additive and dominance variances (1 for inbred lines).

Value

An object of class "ad_diallel".

Details

The combining-ability analysis is on the scale of entry means: the error is the error mean square of the trial divided by the number of replicates. Rows that do not belong to the method are left out (parents in methods 3 and 4; reciprocals in methods 2 and 4, where the cross with the first parent as female is kept), so one data set serves all methods. The effects are the least-squares estimates under Griffing's restrictions (sum of GCA effects zero; SCA effects summing to zero for every parent, the selfs counted twice in method 2), which reproduce his closed formulas.

References

Griffing, B. (1956) Australian Journal of Biological Sciences 9, 463-493. Cockerham, C. C. (1963) In Statistical Genetics and Plant Breeding, NAS-NRC 982, 53-94.

Examples

dl <- diallel(maize_diallel, "Yield_t_ha", "Female", "Male", block = "Block", method = 1)
dl
